thread:
samir: FYI support triage — FLYR on renewal asked for a console view that shows per-tenant cost + latency drilldown by route and an easy trace link to the request. They said this is a gating item for their contract renewal. asked: CSV export, token-level cost breakdown, ability to filter by model variant and time window.

maya: +1. can you paste the customer's raw ask? important to know whether they need every request-level trace or just sampled traces. :eyes:

samir: pasted below from support — short version: "need per-customer chargeback dashboard, per-route breakdown, clickable trace link that opens tracing UI with prefilled trace id, and ability to export for finance. ideally hourly rollups and ability to isolate embedding vs generation costs."

lina: quick question — do they need the trace link to include the exact token offsets/KV cache info, or just the high-level request id? including token offsets is a big lift.

samir: they asked for "trace link to the request" so i read that as request id -> open trace. not token offsets. finance wants token-level cost columns in export though (tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd).

maya: proposes scope for MVP: (1) per-tenant + per-route hourly rollups, (2) export CSV with tokens_in/tokens_out/cost_usd, (3) trace link that opens traces UI filtered by request id, (4) model-variant filter. defer sampled request-level viewer (full raw requests) to next phase. anyone object?
devon: sounds reasonable. we should add launch criteria: accuracy within 5% for cost calc (matching billing), ability to filter at least 90 days, perf SLOs — dashboard load < 2s for 30-day view for tenants with <= 1M tokens.
lina: dependency note: tracing link needs small API change from eng-infra: traces accept query param trace_id->prefill. ops-bot: deploy ticket created: #ENGINF-4821 (needs eng-infra owner).

maya: timeline ask from sales: they want an ETA to give to customer. we should decide whether to pull into next sprint or backlog. impact/effort: product-facing UX + export (med), backend aggregation and cost attribution (med-high), traces param (low). any prioritization guidance?
devon: map to our OKRs: cost visibility is in Q2 roadmap but not in current sprint. if this helps a renewal, we can treat as high-priority customer-driven. trade: cut token-level per-row detail from MVP if timeboxed — keep tokens aggregated by hour.

samir: sales asked for a conservative ETA of 4–6 weeks. is that realistic if we scope to MVP (hourly rollups + CSV + trace link)?
lina: engineering note: 4–6 weeks is tight but doable if we scope properly and we don't need schema migration. we can add a migration later for per-request export.
maya: decision: customer-driven priority OK, MVP scope = hourly rollups + CSV with token aggregates + trace link + model variant filter. launch criteria: (a) cost numbers match billing within 5% on sample tenants, (b) CSV export tested with finance, (c) dashboard loads <2s for 30-day sample, (d) tracing link opens trace in single click. go/no-go will be signoff by product + eng + sales.
samir: will reply to sales with scoped ETA 5 weeks and note that row-level per-request export is tbd. will update the support ticket with scope and link to this thread.
maya: thx — i'll create a product spec doc and attach acceptance tests. please add any edge cases here.
devon: edge case: multi-model routes where embeddings and generation happen in one request — need clear attribution rules (split cost proportionally by tokens_in/out?). add to spec.
lina: operational concern: retention — will storing hourly rollups for >90 days be included in infra cost? product should decide retention default and paid retention tiers.
maya: noted. i'll add retention policy options: 30d default, 90d enterprise tier, export archived data on request.
samir: sales will want a demo — let's aim for an internal demo at week 4. ops-bot: calendar invite created: "Console cost drilldown demo" 2026-04-15 10:00 UTC. :calendar:

maya: will mock a demo dashboard screenshot and attach in spec. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: closure note: thread labeled #customer-request, assigned to product (maya) and eng-infra (lina)."
